fields.description:
## Context / Problem

Escaped-bug analysis (ticket `cranial-goodly-seahog`) found four regressions in which a newly
added hard-fail CI gate/floor/cap broke branches that were already in flight or that predated
the gate: `medium-loved-newt` (a Git-version floor gate hard-failed in-flight changes),
`impudent-sodium-ferret` (new gate steps failed pre-gate changes), `rancid-aerophobic-skylark`
(a module-size cap broke `main`), and `brattish-ladyish-jaguar` (unguarded gate steps, where a
correct code-review finding was dropped because the Pass-2 verifier could not reason about
gate-step semantics). rebar's code-review gate has no criterion that looks at a pipeline /
gate-configuration change and asks whether a branch created before that change would now fail,
so authors keep landing ungrandfathered gates and the review passes.

## Approach

Ship a project-owned **advisory** code-review criterion `project.ci-gate-compat` following the
existing `project.review-phase-boundaries` dogfood pattern — routing in
`.rebar/criteria_routing.json`, the Pass-1 rubric in `.rebar/prompts/`, the eval corpus in
`.rebar/evals/`, documented under `docs/llm-framework.md` "Project dogfood" — so the shared,
shipped gate never carries this project's invariant.

Trigger it through the **declarative `applies_to` glob seam** the routing index already
defines (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` `applies_to_globs` and
`glob_triggered_overlays`), never a hard-coded `.github/workflows/**` test in Python. A
CI-vendor-specific code path would break `project.portability`'s support-matrix cell "CI under
any provider (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, and others), projects with NO CI provider at
all". With the glob seam, adding another CI system is adding a glob, not editing code. The
shipped glob set is `**/.github/workflows/**`, `**/Jenkinsfile*`, `**/.gitlab-ci.yml`,
`**/.circleci/**`, `**/azure-pipelines*.y*ml`, `**/.buildkite/**`,
`**/bitbucket-pipelines.yml`, `**/.drone.yml`.

Two code changes are required, because activated project code-review criteria are today
injected **unconditionally**: `_activated_code_review_project_criteria`
(`src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py`) returns every activated `project.` id, and
`CodeReviewBatchRunner.run` (`src/rebar/llm/code_review/batch_runner.py`) runs each one in the
Round-A fan-in with no reference to `applies_to`.

1. **Gate project criteria on their globs.** Filter the activated project criteria by their
   effective `applies_to` globs against the review's changed files, which are already threaded
   to the call site as `prep.dc.changed_files` in `gate_dispatch.py`, reusing the existing
   matcher `registry._glob_match` (which delegates to
   `rebar._engine_support.commit_impact.glob_match`). An **empty** `applies_to` keeps today's
   always-on behaviour, so the already-shipped `project.review-phase-boundaries` is unchanged.
2. **Make the glob set project-overridable.** A routing entry may declare
   `applies_to_config_key`, a dotted config path whose non-empty list value **replaces** that
   criterion's `applies_to`. `project.ci-gate-compat` declares `code_review.ci_config_globs`,
   and a new core config section `[code_review]` gains `ci_config_globs: list[str]`, modelled
   on `CodeHealthConfig.scan_roots` / `include_extensions` in `src/rebar/_config_schema.py`
   (registered in `Config` and `_SECTION_CLASSES` there). The pointer is declarative so the
   shipped package never names a project-owned criterion id, and a project with an unusual
   pipeline declares its own paths instead of waiting for rebar to enumerate them.

Rationale for this approach: it reuses the two mechanisms rebar already has for exactly this
job — the `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` criteria overlay and the `applies_to` glob trigger —
instead of introducing a new trigger kind; it keeps the invariant in project-owned `.rebar/`
files where the project can retune it; and it satisfies portability by naming no CI vendor in
either shipped code or the rubric text.

The rubric asks a CI-agnostic question — "does this pipeline/gate-configuration change
introduce a hard-fail step or required gate with no if-present / grandfather guard, so a branch
created before this change would fail?" — and uses no GitHub-specific vocabulary.

Ship **advisory** (`default_posture: advisory`, `blocking_enabled: false`,
`block_threshold: 0.90`), the same posture the `project.review-phase-boundaries` dogfood
shipped with, so the criterion is calibrated on real reviews first; flipping it to blocking is
deliberately out of scope for this ticket and is a separate, calibration-gated change.

## Scope

Project-owned criterion assets:

- `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` — add the `code_review` → `project.ci-gate-compat` routing
  entry (`exec: 1-TURN`, advisory, `blocking_enabled: false`, `block_threshold: 0.90`, the
  eight-glob `applies_to`, `applies_to_config_key: "code_review.ci_config_globs"`) and its
  `activate` entry.
- `.rebar/prompts/code-review-project-ci-gate-compat.md` — new Pass-1 rubric
  (`outputs: code_review_findings`, `execution_mode: single_turn`,
  `category: code-review-pass`, `dimension: ci-gate-compat`), CI-agnostic wording.
- `.rebar/evals/code-review-project-ci-gate-compat.eval.yaml` — new balanced eval spec
  (six fire cases `CG-F1`–`CG-F6`, six pass cases `CG-N1`–`CG-N6`, matching gold set).
- `.gitignore` — add the two `!`-unignore lines for the new prompt and eval files, next to the
  existing `code-review-project-review-phase-boundaries` lines.

Shipped code (the glob-trigger seam and its config override):

- `src/rebar/_config_sections.py` — add the `"code_review"` entry to `_SECTIONS` with
  `"ci_config_globs": lambda v, k: _as_str_list(v, k)`, mirroring the `"code_health"` entry.
- `src/rebar/_config_schema.py` — new `CodeReviewConfig` dataclass with
  `ci_config_globs: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)` carrying a `# read-via:` marker
  (required by `scripts/check_config_reads.py`, run from `make lint`), wired into `Config` and
  `_SECTION_CLASSES`.
- `src/rebar/config.py` — re-export `CodeReviewConfig` alongside the other section classes.
- `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` — new `project_applies_to_globs(criterion_id,
  repo_root)` resolving the effective globs: the `applies_to_config_key` value read off
  `config.compose_config(repo_root)` when non-empty, else the routing `applies_to`. Reading
  composed config from `rebar/llm` is the established seam (`config.compose_config(repo_root)`
  is already used in `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pin_health.py` and
  `src/rebar/llm/completion.py`), so `scripts/check_config_ownership.py` stays clean.
- `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py` — `_activated_code_review_project_criteria` takes
  the changed files and drops a project criterion whose non-empty effective globs match none of
  them; its call site passes `prep.dc.changed_files`.

Docs and tests:

- `docs/llm-framework.md` — new "Project dogfood: ci-gate-compat" section.
- `docs/config.md` — document `[code_review] ci_config_globs`, copying the
  "Code-health analyzers (`code_health.*`)" section's shape (prose, a `rebar.toml` block, a
  `pyproject.toml` block, then the per-key type/default paragraph).
- `tests/golden/config_surface.json` — add `code_review.ci_config_globs` to `config_keys` and
  `REBAR_CODE_REVIEW_CI_CONFIG_GLOBS` to `canonical_env_vars`.
- `tests/unit/test_project_ci_gate_compat.py` — new offline contract tests for the criterion
  assets, the glob gating, and the config override.

## Testing

All tests are offline (no live model call): the criterion's assets are asserted as data, and
the dispatch behaviour is asserted through the existing injected-runner seams.

- **Happy path** — a diff whose changed files include a pipeline-config path selects
  `project.ci-gate-compat` into the Round-A criteria set; the rubric loads through
  `prompts.get_prompt` with `outputs == "code_review_findings"` and
  `execution_mode == "single_turn"`; the eval spec passes `validate_eval_spec(strict=True)`
  and is balanced 6/6.
- **Negative / edge path** — a diff that touches **no** pipeline-config path drops
  `project.ci-gate-compat` from the Round-A set (asserted through the recording runner, which
  must record zero dispatches for its prompt id), while `project.review-phase-boundaries`,
  whose `applies_to` is empty, is still dispatched — the regression guard for change 1.
- **Config-override path** — with `[code_review] ci_config_globs` set to a project-specific
  path (e.g. `["ci/pipeline.yaml"]`), a diff touching only that path selects the criterion and
  a diff touching only `.github/workflows/ci.yml` does not, proving the config value replaces
  rather than extends the shipped globs; with the key unset, the shipped globs apply.
- **Empty-changed-files edge** — a review with an empty changed-file list drops every
  glob-gated project criterion and raises no error.
- **Perfect-solver calibration contract** — `calibrate_criterion` over the new eval corpus with
  an injected perfect solver reports `recall == 1.0` and `false_accept == 0.0`, mirroring the
  `project.review-phase-boundaries` contract test.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar.llm.code_review.registry.effective_criteria(<repo root>)` contains
      `project.ci-gate-compat`, and its routing entry reads `exec: "1-TURN"`,
      `default_posture: "advisory"`, `blocking_enabled: false`, `block_threshold: 0.90` —
      verified by an assertion in `tests/unit/test_project_ci_gate_compat.py`.
- [ ] The routing entry's `applies_to` is exactly the eight globs listed in Scope and no
      shipped Python file under `src/rebar/` contains the literal `.github/workflows` as a
      criterion trigger for this criterion — verified by an assertion in the new test plus
      `grep -rn "github/workflows" src/rebar/` returning no new match.
- [ ] The rubric at `.rebar/prompts/code-review-project-ci-gate-compat.md` loads via
      `prompts.get_prompt` with `outputs == "code_review_findings"`,
      `execution_mode == "single_turn"`, and its body contains none of the vendor strings
      `github`, `gitlab`, `jenkins`, `circleci`, `buildkite`, `bitbucket`, `drone`
      (case-insensitive) — verified by an assertion in the new test.
- [ ] A code review whose changed files include a pipeline-config path dispatches the
      `code-review-project-ci-gate-compat` prompt, and one whose changed files include none
      does not, while `project.review-phase-boundaries` (empty `applies_to`) is dispatched in
      both — verified by the recording-runner assertions described in Testing.
- [ ] Setting `[code_review] ci_config_globs = ["ci/pipeline.yaml"]` makes a change to
      `ci/pipeline.yaml` select the criterion and a change to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` not
      select it — verified by a test that builds the config value and asserts both directions.
- [ ] `rebar.llm.evals.eval.validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True) == []` for the new eval spec,
      the dataset is twelve cases split 6 fire / 6 pass, and `calibrate_criterion` with an
      injected perfect solver reports `recall == 1.0` and `false_accept == 0.0` — verified by
      assertions in the new test.
- [ ] `docs/llm-framework.md` contains a "Project dogfood: ci-gate-compat" section naming the
      advisory posture and the `CG-F1`/`CG-N6` corpus bounds, and `docs/config.md` documents
      `[code_review] ci_config_globs` — verified by a docs assertion in the new test.
- [ ] `tests/golden/config_surface.json` lists `code_review.ci_config_globs` and
      `REBAR_CODE_REVIEW_CI_CONFIG_GLOBS`, and `python -m pytest
      tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py` exits 0 — verified by running that test.
- [ ] `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint` and `... make typecheck` both exit 0 in the
      worktree (this covers `scripts/check_config_reads.py`,
      `scripts/check_config_ownership.py`, and the complexity ratchet), and
      `... python -m pytest tests/unit/test_project_ci_gate_compat.py
      tests/unit/test_code_review_project_criteria.py
      tests/unit/test_project_review_phase_boundaries.py
      tests/unit/test_config_surface_golden.py tests/unit/test_config_loader.py` exits 0.
